providers.name: Spotify Web API
notes: All endpoints share the host https://api.spotify.com and require an OAuth 2.0 access token in an Authorization: Bearer header.
Catalog endpoints (albums, artists, tracks, search) accept an app-only Client Credentials token. Endpoints under /v1/me require a user token with the listed scopes.

February 2026 Development Mode changes: owner must have Spotify Premium; new apps limited to 5 users; many bulk/browse/user endpoints removed; several response fields removed (album label/popularity/available_markets, track popularity/available_markets/linked_from, artist followers/popularity, several user profile fields); playlist 'tracks' renamed 'items' and playlist contents restricted to playlists the user owns or collaborates on; search limit max reduced to 10.

Removed endpoints (for example Get Artist's Top Tracks, Get New Releases, Get Several Albums, GET /v1/users/{id}/playlists, GET /v1/playlists/{id}/tracks) are intentionally excluded from this library.
Response samples model a Development Mode app: removed fields are omitted from samples but listed in responseFields as deprecated with a note.
Image URLs for playlist images are temporary and expire in less than a day.
Developer policy: Spotify content may not be downloaded, cover art must be shown in original form with a link back to Spotify, and content may not be used to train ML/AI models.

expansionNotes: Re-verified 2026-10-17: Web API changelog pages exist for February, March, May and July 2026; no later changelog page was found.
May 2026: account_id was added to the User object returned by Get Current User's Profile; Spotify recommends account_id (stable, pseudonymous) instead of id for linking accounts.
July 2026: a developer may create up to 25 Client IDs (was 1); Development Mode quotas are counted per developer account rather than per Client ID, so several Development Mode apps share one quota.
July 2026: a 429 Too Many Requests response caused by an exceeded quota carries an error object whose reason is QUOTA_EXCEEDED.

February 2026 library consolidation: the type-specific save/remove/contains/follow endpoints were replaced by PUT /v1/me/library, DELETE /v1/me/library and GET /v1/me/library/contains, which take Spotify URIs (max 40). The GET list endpoints for saved tracks (/v1/me/tracks), saved albums (/v1/me/albums) and followed artists (/v1/me/following) remain.
Playlists are created with POST /v1/me/playlists (POST /v1/users/{user_id}/playlists was removed) and items are added with POST /v1/playlists/{playlist_id}/items (the /tracks variant was removed).
Apps in Extended Quota Mode are not affected by the February 2026 Development Mode changes (migration guide); this library models a Development Mode app.

providers.name: YouTube Data API v3
notes: All endpoints share the host https://www.googleapis.com and the path prefix /youtube/v3.
Every list method requires a part parameter. part selects which top-level groups of properties (snippet, contentDetails, statistics, ...) appear in each resource; unrequested parts are absent.
Public data can be read with an API key (key query parameter). Write operations and private data require OAuth 2.0 user authorization.

Quota (getting-started page, verified 2026-10-17): 100 search.list calls per day in a separate Search Queries bucket, plus 10,000 units per day for all other endpoints combined. The list methods in this library cost 1 unit per call.
Count statistics (viewCount, likeCount, commentCount, subscriberCount, videoCount) are unsigned long values serialized as JSON strings; convert before doing arithmetic.
dislikeCount has been private since December 13, 2021, and favoriteCount is deprecated (always 0).
Video durations use ISO 8601 duration strings such as PT15M33S.
standard and maxres thumbnails are not available for every video.

providers.name: Google Maps Platform
notes: Google Maps Platform is a family of separate APIs. Each endpoint here names its actual service: Places API (New), Routes API, Geocoding API, or Directions API (Legacy). Each must be enabled separately in a Cloud project with billing.

Places API (New) and Routes API require a response field mask (X-Goog-FieldMask header). Omitting it returns an error. The fields requested also determine the billing tier (Essentials, Pro, Enterprise, Enterprise + Atmosphere).
Search responses wrap results in a places array, so search field masks use a places. prefix; Place Details returns a single Place, so its mask has no prefix.

Places API (legacy), Directions API and Distance Matrix API were given Legacy status on March 1, 2025 (replacements: Places API (New) and Routes API). Google's legacy overview says legacy services are not available in new Cloud projects; the Directions page itself states that as of October 2026 Directions API (Legacy) can no longer be enabled for new projects. Cut-off details are per product, so check each product page. The library includes Directions (Legacy) only as a clearly flagged distractor.
Photo resource names from Places responses cannot be cached and may expire. Author attributions must be displayed with photos.
Routes API durations are strings of seconds with an 's' suffix ("1150s"); distanceMeters is always meters regardless of units.
Geocoding is modeled with the v3 web-service format; the documentation notes that Geocoding API v4 is generally available.

flaws.explanation: Slash commands are interactions that Discord delivers to the app (here, to its Interactions Endpoint URL); they are not channel messages to poll, and there is no REST route to list interactions. Polling every 2 seconds also wastes rate-limit budget, and without MESSAGE_CONTENT the content of other users' messages comes back empty anyway.
Create Message posts an ordinary channel message; it does not answer the interaction, so the command is never acknowledged within the 3-second deadline.

Create Message flags can only be SUPPRESS_EMBEDS, SUPPRESS_NOTIFICATIONS, IS_VOICE_MESSAGE or IS_COMPONENTS_V2, so the reply would be visible to everyone. Only an interaction response can set EPHEMERAL (64).
Nothing records the reply's ID. The interaction callback returns it only when with_response=true (interaction.response_message_id).

Without with_response=true the callback returns 204 No Content, so the reply ID for the log is missing.

Interactions must be answered within 3 seconds using the interaction's own id and token; the token stays valid for 15 minutes for follow-ups.
Ephemeral replies exist only for interaction responses (flag 64).
An optional parameter (with_response) changes 204 No Content into a JSON body with interaction.response_message_id.
Without MESSAGE_CONTENT, reading other users' message text returns empty strings, so a polling design would fail even before rate limits.
